title: Mom's Shopping List
text:
Mom wrote this shopping list and stuck it on the fridge. I helped by adding a few things when she was not looking.

Mom's list: milk, eggs, bread, twelve bananas, cheese, soap for the dishes, a big bag of {plural noun}, and exactly {number} jars of jam.

My list: a {adjective} balloon, something {color} for the cat, a box of {plural noun}, and a giant {noun} for my baby brother.

At the store, Mom found my part of the list. She laughed {adverb} and said I could pick one thing. I picked the balloon. Then she let me push the cart, and I {past tense verb} all the way down the cereal aisle.

When we got home, Mom said I was a great helper. Next week she wants me to {verb} the whole list by myself. I am going to write it {adverb} so she can read it.

title: The Day I Pushed the Cart
text:
Dear Diary,

Today Dad took me to the grocery store, and for the first time ever, I got to push the cart all by myself.

The cart had one wheel that squeaked {adverb} no matter what I did. Dad said every cart has one wheel like that. We started in the fruit section, where I picked out six apples and a {adjective} pineapple.

Next we went to the dairy aisle. Dad needed milk, yogurt, and a block of cheese the size of a {noun}. I carefully put everything in the cart next to the {plural noun}.

In the cereal aisle, I saw a box with a {animal} on the front. Dad said we could get it if I promised to {verb} after dinner.

At the checkout, the cashier said I was the best cart driver she had seen all day. I {past tense verb} all the way to the car. Next time, Dad says I can help pick out the {plural noun}.

Love,
Owen

title: A Letter to the Store Manager
text:
Dear Store Manager,

My name is Lily. I shop at your store every Sunday with my grandpa. My favorite part is the aisle with all the {plural noun}. I am writing to share some ideas to make your store even better.

Idea one: Every cart should have a little horn that goes "{sound}" so people know you are coming.

Idea two: Please play more music in the store. I think shoppers would love to {verb} in the frozen food aisle. It would keep them warm.

Idea three: You should sell {adjective} bananas. The yellow ones are nice, but kids like surprises.

Idea four: The person who gives out free samples should also give out {plural noun}. Grandpa agrees with this one.

Also, thank you to Miss Rosa at the checkout. She always smiles and talks {adverb} to me. Last week she gave me a sticker of a {noun}, and I put it on my lunchbox.

Thank you for reading my letter. I hope you will think about my ideas while you are {verb ending in ing}.

Your friend,
Lily

title: Where to Find It at Corner Market
text:

Aisle one: Fruits and vegetables. Our tomatoes are red and our carrots are {color}. Please ask before you take a free grape.

Aisle two: Bread and cereal. The top shelf has the {adjective} bread that Mrs. Hall likes.

Aisle three: Milk, eggs, and cheese. This aisle is very cold, so we keep a {noun} there for anyone who needs to warm up.

Aisle four: Soup, beans, and {plural noun}. Everything here comes in a can.

Aisle five: Paper towels, soap, and sponges. Our helper, Ben, likes to {verb} in this aisle when the store is quiet.

Aisle six: Snacks and treats. Please walk {adverb} here, because this is where the {plural noun} live.

If you still cannot find what you need, look for someone in a green apron. They will help you {adverb} and happily. Or just shout "{exclamation}!" and our manager will come {verb ending in ing} to help you.

title: Help Wanted at Green Leaf Grocery
text:
Green Leaf Grocery is looking for a new helper! Please read about the job below.

Job title: Shelf Stacker

What you will do: Put cans, boxes, and jars on the shelves in neat rows. Make sure the soup is next to the soup and the crackers are next to the crackers. Never put the {plural noun} on the cookie shelf.

You must be able to: Lift a box of {plural noun}, smile at every customer, and {verb} when the radio plays a good song.

You will wear: A green apron, a name tag, and a {adjective} hat.

Best part of the job: Every afternoon, all the helpers share a snack of {food} in the break room.

Hardest part of the job: The top shelf. Our tallest helper, Maria, can reach it, but she always {past tense verb} when she does.

To apply, come to the front desk and tell our manager why you would be a {adjective} helper. Please speak {adverb}, because she is usually {verb ending in ing} in the back.

title: Rules for Being a Store Helper
text:
My family goes to the grocery store every Friday. Mom says I am her official helper, so here are the helper rules.

Rule one: Stay close to the cart. If you stop to look at the {plural noun} for too long, Mom will make you hold the list.

Rule two: Only put things in the cart that are on the list. Last week I put a {adjective} {noun} in the cart, and Mom found it at the checkout.

Rule three: Use your inside voice. If you need to sneeze, sneeze {adverb} into your elbow.

Rule four: Help carry the bags. I can carry the bread, the eggs, and a bag of {plural noun} all at once.

Rule five: Say thank you to the cashier. Our cashier, Mr. Ray, always says "{silly word}!" back to me.

Rule six: If you are a very good helper, you get to {verb} on the way home. Today I was the best helper ever, so I {past tense verb} the whole way while {verb ending in ing}.

title: My Interview with Ms. Bell
text:
For my class project, I interviewed Ms. Bell, the cashier at our grocery store. Here is what she said.

Question: How long have you worked here?
Ms. Bell: For {number} years. I started when this store was just a tiny {noun}.

Question: What is the best part of your job?
Ms. Bell: Meeting nice people. One man comes in every day and buys only {plural noun}. He is very {adjective}.

Question: What is the funniest thing you ever scanned?
Ms. Bell: A pumpkin that looked just like a {animal}. Everyone in line {past tense verb}.

Question: What do you do on your break?
Ms. Bell: I like to {verb} in the back room and eat a sandwich with {plural noun} in it.

Question: Do you have any advice for kids?
Ms. Bell: Always bag the eggs {adverb} and put the bread on top. And never stop {verb ending in ing}.

Thank you, Ms. Bell! You are the most {adjective} cashier in the whole town.
